title: TSMC and Sony Form $4.7 Billion Joint Venture for Next-Gen Image Sensors
excerpt: The two tech giants will invest a combined 747 billion yen to develop advanced image sensors in southern Japan, with volume production expected to begin in 2029.
body:
• TSMC and Sony Group will form a $4.69 billion joint venture called Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp, based in Kumamoto, Japan
  • Sony will invest $2.92 billion as the controlling shareholder while TSMC contributes $1.77 billion, with volume production of next-generation image sensors targeted for 2029
  • The partnership marks Sony's shift toward a "fab-light" manufacturing model and will explore AI applications in automotive and robotics beyond smartphone sensors

TSMC and Sony Group announced Tuesday they will form a $4.69 billion joint venture to develop and manufacture next-generation image sensors in southern Japan, deepening an existing partnership between the world's largest contract chipmaker and the dominant force in image sensor technology.

The new entity, named Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp, will be headquartered in Kumamoto prefecture, where TSMC already operates its Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing (JASM) chip plant. Volume production is expected to begin in 2029, according to a joint statement from the companies.

The Deal Structure

Sony will serve as the controlling shareholder, investing 465 billion yen ($2.92 billion) through a combination of cash and asset transfers, including its newly constructed chip factory in Kumamoto's Koshi City. TSMC will contribute 282 billion yen ($1.77 billion), bringing total capital to 747 billion yen.

https://x.com/StockMKTNewz/status/2087142605377142989

Capital contributions will be phased according to market demand and other business conditions. The companies noted that additional funding needed to reach planned production capacity is being considered "on the assumption that Japanese government support will be available," according to Reuters. Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry has already committed up to 60 billion yen (roughly $380 million) in subsidies for Sony's image sensor facility in Kumamoto.

A Nikkei report on Monday had pegged total spending at around 1 trillion yen ($6.3 billion), suggesting the combined investment including government subsidies could significantly exceed the companies' initial capital commitments.

A Strategic Shift for Sony

Under the partnership, Sony will lead development of core image sensor technologies along with product planning and design, while the venture draws on TSMC's advanced process technology and large-scale manufacturing expertise.

"The joint venture with TSMC will be our first step to becoming fab-light. Until now, we have handled everything in-house, from R&D to manufacturing, but going forward, we hope to advance manufacturing not only on our own but also by bringing in partners."

— Hiroki Totoki, Sony CEO

The move represents a significant strategic pivot for Sony, which has historically kept its entire sensor operation — from research and development to fabrication — under one roof. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki has signaled a broader shift toward an intellectual-property-focused model, similar to the company's recent decision to partner its Bravia television line with TCL, according to Bloomberg.

Beyond Smartphones: The AI Play

While the joint venture's immediate focus is smartphone image sensors, both companies have been clear about broader ambitions. The partnership will explore opportunities in what they call "physical AI" applications, including automotive sensing and robotics.

"This partnership underscores our shared commitment and mutual vision of leveraging cutting-edge technologies and innovative solutions to deliver leading sensing technology and products."

— Dr. Kevin Zhang, TSMC Senior Vice President and Deputy Co-COO

Sony has been pushing on-chip intelligence since it unveiled the IMX500 Intelligent Vision sensor in 2020, and the Kumamoto venture appears designed as the manufacturing platform for that next generation — stacked sensors combining logic, memory, and AI inference on a single device.

TSMC's Dr. Kevin Zhang called the partnership "a key step forward in driving future sensing technology in the AI era" at the original MOU signing in May.

Building on an Existing Foundation

The two companies are not starting from scratch. TSMC and Sony already share a joint venture through JASM, established in 2021 and majority-owned by TSMC. JASM's first fab in Kumamoto began volume production in late 2024, supplying logic chips to Sony and automotive supplier DENSO using 22/28nm and 12/16nm process technologies. TSMC has since decided to upgrade its second Kumamoto fab to 3nm capability.

Sony is the world's largest maker of CMOS image sensors, supplying chips used in smartphones from Apple, Samsung, and others, as well as automotive cameras. TSMC manufactures chips for many of the world's largest technology companies, including Apple, Nvidia, and AMD.

What's Next

The formal establishment of Advanced Vision Semiconductor Manufacturing Corp remains subject to a definitive legally binding agreement and customary closing conditions. With production not expected until 2029, the venture's timeline aligns with anticipated growth in AI-driven demand for advanced sensing technology across multiple industries.

For Sony, the partnership could reshape how the company approaches semiconductor manufacturing, potentially freeing up capital for its entertainment and content businesses while maintaining its technological edge in image sensing. The success of this "fab-light" model may determine whether Sony extends the approach to other parts of its semiconductor division.
image_caption: TSMC and Sony have announced a $4.69 billion joint venture in Kumamoto, Japan, to manufacture next-generation image sensors. Volume production is targeted for 2029, with Sony as the controlling shareholder.
